questions.q: Who did Yahweh tell Moses to count in the census?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to count every man of Israel who was 20 years old or older and could go out to war.

questions.q: Who would serve Moses as tribe leaders?
questions.a: A man from every tribe, the head of his ancestral family, would serve as his tribe’s leader.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Reuben who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Elizur, the son of Shedeur, was the leader from the tribe of Reuben.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Simeon who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Shelumiel, the son of Zurishaddai, was the leader from the tribe of Simeon.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Judah who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Nahshon, the son of Amminadab, was the leader from the tribe of Judah.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Issachar who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Nethanel, the son of Zuar, was the leader from the tribe of Issachar.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Zebulun who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Eliab, the son of Helon, was the leader from the tribe of Zebulun.

questions.q: Who were the leaders from the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh?
questions.a: Elishama, the son of Ammihud, was the leader from Ephraim, and Gamaliel, the son of Pedahzur, was the leader from Manasseh.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Benjamin who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Abidan, the son of Gideoni, was the leader from the tribe of Benjamin.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Dan who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Ahiezer, the son of Ammishaddai, was the leader from the tribe of Dan.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Asher who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Pagiel, the son of Okran, was the leader from the tribe of Asher.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Gad who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Eliasaph, the son of Deuel, was the leader from the tribe of Gad.

questions.q: Who was the leader from the tribe of Naphtali who would stand with Moses and Aaron?
questions.a: Ahira, the son of Enan, was the leader from the tribe of Naphtali.

questions.q: What position did the men named in verses 5-15 hold in Israel?
questions.a: They were the leaders of their tribes, and they led the clans of Israel.

questions.q: Which men did Moses and Aaron take?
questions.a: They took the men whose names Yahweh had listed.

questions.q: How did each man record his ancestry?
questions.a: Each man registered themselves by name, one by one, according to his tribal group and his ancestral family.

questions.q: Where did Moses count the men?
questions.a: He counted them in the wilderness of Sinai.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Reuben were counted?
questions.a: 46,500 men of the tribe of Reuben were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Simeon were counted?
questions.a: 59,300 men of the tribe of Simeon were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Gad were counted?
questions.a: 45,650 men of the tribe of Gad were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Judah were counted?
questions.a: 74,600 men of the tribe of Judah were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Issachar were counted?
questions.a: 54,400 men of the tribe of Issachar were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Zebulun were counted?
questions.a: 57,400 men of the tribe of Zebulun were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Ephraim were counted?
questions.a: 40,500 men of the tribe of Ephraim were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Manasseh were counted?
questions.a: 32,200 men of the tribe of Manasseh were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Benjamin were counted?
questions.a: 35,400 men of the tribe of Benjamin were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Dan were counted?
questions.a: 62,700 men of the tribe of Dan were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Asher were counted?
questions.a: 41,500 men of the tribe of Asher were counted.

questions.q: How many men of the tribe of Naphtali were counted?
questions.a: 53,400 men of the tribe of Naphtali were counted.

questions.q: How many leaders of Israel helped Moses and Aaron count the men?
questions.a: Twelve leaders helped them, one man for each ancestral family.

questions.q: Which men of Israel were counted according to their ancestral families?
questions.a: All the men who were 20 years old or older and could go out to war in Israel were counted.

questions.q: How many men 20 years old or older who could go out to war were counted?
questions.a: There were 603,550 men counted.

questions.q: Which tribe was not counted with the other tribes?
questions.a: The Levites were not counted with the other tribes.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses about the tribe of Levi?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses not to count the tribe of Levi among the sons of Israel.

questions.q: What were the Levites assigned to care for?
questions.a: They were assigned to care for the Dwelling of the Testimony, all its vessels, and everything that belongs to it.

questions.q: What would happen to any stranger who came near the Dwelling?
questions.a: That stranger would be put to death.

questions.q: Where were the people of Israel to set up their tents?
questions.a: Each man was to set up his tent by his own banner, according to his army division.

questions.q: Where were the Levites to set up their tents?
questions.a: They were to set up their tents around the Dwelling of the Testimony.

questions.q: Did the people do what Yahweh commanded?
questions.a: Yes, the people of Israel did everything that Yahweh commanded Moses.

commentary.text: The Levites not numbered with the rest.

Verses 1–43 The people were numbered to show God's faithfulness in thus increasing the seed of Jacob, that they might be the better trained for the wars and conquest of Canaan, and to ascertain their families in order to the division of the land. It is said of each tribe, that those were numbered who were able to go forth to war; they had wars before them, though now they met with no opposition. Let the believer be prepared to withstand the enemies of his soul, though all may appear to be peace.

We have here the sum total. How much was required to maintain all these in the wilderness! They were all provided for by God every day. When we observe the faithfulness of God, however unlikely the performance of his promise may appear, we may take courage as to those which yet remain to be fulfilled to the church of God.

Care is here taken to distinguish the tribe of Levi, which, in the matter of the golden calf, had distinguished itself. Singular services shall be recompensed by singular honours. It was to the honour of the Levites, that to them was committed the care of the tabernacle and its treasures, in their camps and in their marches. It was for the honour of the holy things that none should see them, or touch them, but those who were called of God to the service. We all are unfit and unworthy to have fellowship with God, till called by his grace into the fellowship of his Son Jesus Christ our Lord; and so, being the spiritual seed of that great High Priest, we are made priests to our God. Great care must be taken to prevent sin, for preventing sin is preventing wrath. Being a holy tribe, they were not reckoned among other Israelites. They that minister about holy things, should neither entangle themselves, nor be entangled, in worldly affairs. And let every believer seek to do what the Lord has commanded.
